en.title: Suspicious Users in Transaction Logs
en.description:
Each log is sender recipient amount. A user is counted once for a log whenever they take part in it as the sender or the recipient; a transfer to oneself still counts only once. Output the ID of every user who takes part in at least threshold logs, sorted in ascending numeric order, not lexicographic string order. The amount does not affect the count.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and numeric ranges missing from the original text are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n threshold, followed by n lines of sender recipient amount. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤threshold≤n; each field is a positive decimal integer of 1..9 digits without leading zeros. The original text guarantees that at least one user is output.
en.output: First output the number of users, then output each user ID in ascending numeric order.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 1
1; 2
2 10; 1
999999999. The examples were checked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: For each log, count the sender first; count the recipient only if it is different. Filter the users who reach the threshold, then sort them as integers.
